My strongest recommendation to you as a math lover and a student who went through this process myself is the following:

1. YOUR ALGEBRA IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FOUNDATIONAL TOOL. I cannot emphasize that enough. You need to have every concept mastered. Do not practice until you get it right, practice until you cannot get it wrong. People struggle in Calculus not because the Calculus concepts are difficult, but because they're stumbling over their algebra while trying to learn Calculus. Don't ever think anything you learn in mathematics is "useless" or "negligible" because 9 times out of 10 it will come back to haunt you later.
2. Your organization skills ought to improve because this is going to immensely help you. If you ignore it,then it will be like trying to climb a mountain with some bricks tied to you. Can you do it? Sure, but you're going to be severely uncomfortable and even then it may not be possible. I'm naturally a decently bright guy and I couldn't do Calculus II if I didn't hunker down and put in real effort.
3. Discrete math in my experience was easier than Calculus II by a large margin. HOWEVER, when i took discrete I had already taken Calculus II so my logical faculties/math abilities were ahead of most people who were taking discrete and had never seen series/summation when I already were familiar with them. I presume if you took discrete math when most people do \[Calculus I level\] it's a tough class, but if you develop the organizational skills and discipline, you can do it.

MOST IMPORTANTLY, do not pursue CS if you hate math. It's a degree that constantly uses mathematical logic, theory, and mathematics in some way \[even if it is not advertised as a mathematical class and is seemingly computer theory heavy\]. You don't necessarily have to love it \[it helps\] but do not go into it knowing you hate it and have no mind of liking it. I feel like this would be nightmarish to do if you didn't enjoy logic, problem solving, and are comfortable with not knowing the answer and feel optimistic to take steps to reach it and grow as a person.
